correctness.rationale: For a²≠4 the six nonzero roots are simple by separability of x↦x³ and the discriminant of u²+au+1; the root at zero is simple. The order-three and reflection actions yield the displayed elliptic quotients. Pullbacks of their regular forms and that of the conjugate reflection span the three-dimensional differential space (the last two are ω₂−ω₀ and ζω₂−ζ²ω₀). The induced norm map is thus an isogeny to E₀×E₁². Independently enumerating multinomial exponent allocations for all nine genus-three entries and both elliptic coefficients modulo 11 gives antidiagonal entries 5a, a⁵−2a³−3a, 5a; elliptic coefficients are a⁵−2a³−3a and 6a. These can be replayed by summing 5!/(i!j!k!) times the monomial coefficients for i+j+k=5 at the stated target exponents. The middle polynomial factors as a(a²+1)(a²−3); the two symmetric antidiagonal entries survive together whenever nonzero, so semilinear iteration kills no extra dimension. Cartier corank gives the a-numbers and the elliptic ordinary/supersingular factors give the slopes. At a=0, a-number three gives superspeciality. The four distinct nonzero exceptional roots are smooth; precisely ±5 are rational over F₁₁, since −1 is not a square, and ±2 are the two exclusions. Parameter counts are not isomorphism-class counts.
residual_risks: The submitted verifier was inspected, not executed. The isogeny is used only geometrically; no degree prime to 11 or descent claim was inferred.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The earlier superspecial paper uses this full matrix to find common zeros, but the matrix formula is stronger than the stated common-zero application. It determines ordinary and intermediate strata as well.

evidence: At p=11 take (n,m)=(5,1) and t=−a in the older formula. The coefficient of u is 5a and the coefficient of u⁵ is a⁵+20a³+30a=a(a²+1)(a²−3) modulo 11.
Each surviving nonzero block of the prior matrix is semilinearly bijective on its own coordinates. Its rank thus equals stable rank, giving (f,a-number)=(0,3),(2,1),(3,0) on the asserted loci.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: At rank three the polygon is ordinary, and at a-number three the Jacobian is superspecial. At rank two, symmetry supplies two slope-one entries and the remaining two slopes must be 1/2: a nonintegral slope with reduced denominator d requires multiplicity divisible by d. Thus the polygon in the only intermediate case is forced. The rational split is obtained by testing the two quadratics, so the full table is a routine specialization even without the quotient proof.

originality.rationale: The earlier Oct. 25 superspecial-parameter result for this exact pencil already gives the full general-prime Cartier coefficient matrix, including its antidiagonal shape for p≡5 mod 6, and explicit coefficient sums. At p=11 its two entries specialize immediately to 5a and a(a²+1)(a²−3). The earlier formula therefore implies the intermediate rank-two locus and all a-numbers, not just the common-zero locus expressly tabulated there. The Newton table then follows from standard slope constraints in the three ranks that occur. A distinct same-day p=13 record also contains the p=11 elliptic Hasse pair, implying the same rank and Newton data; its date is not used to establish priority.
residual_risks: No exhaustive historical-priority claim is made. Whether a single older table printed all rows together is unresolved and immaterial to the verified general-matrix implication.

value.rationale: The arithmetic strata of this classical pencil are a natural target, but an earlier result already determines the full Cartier matrix for every tame prime. Two elementary coefficient readings at 11 and the forced dimension-three slope types give the reported exact table. The alternative elliptic proof and normalized F₁₁ counts supply confirmations of that specialization, not a distinct mathematical gap or valuable remainder.
